boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Philippi record (June 3, 1861) in Operations in Western Virginia [June-December 1861]. The May 26-30 advance on Grafton and the Confederate withdrawal to Beverly and Huttonsville are context. Campaign-wide movements, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Brigades; the live field reads zero. Morris's orders sent Kelley with six companies of his own regiment, nine of the Ninth Indiana and six of the Sixteenth Ohio, and Dumont with eight companies of the Seventh Indiana joined by five companies and two guns under Steedman and six companies under Crittenden. Nicolay puts Kelley at the head of about two regiments and Porterfield's command at something over a thousand.
claims.rationale: Company counts from orders and a history's round figures; no return for either side on June 3. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live pages list Colonel Thomas A. Morris and Colonel George A. Porterfield; the Official Records style Morris a brigadier general of Indiana militia. Morris says Kelley had organized the expedition before Morris arrived at Grafton, that Morris postponed it a night and issued the orders, that Kelley was wounded leading his column and that Dumont then had command. Nicolay says Morris adopted and completed an expedition projected by Kelley.
claims.rationale: Command roles from an interested report and a history; the listed commanders do not receive automatic sole credit, and no inspected passage describes Porterfield's orders.

open_questions: McClellan's June 3 and June 10 reports, the Confederate Heck-Cowan-Harman and Harman reports, Porterfield's June 9 and 11 reports and the court of inquiry findings (which give about 600 effective infantry and 175 cavalry at Philippi) were read but not selected under the three-family ceiling; Kelley's and Dumont's reports were not read.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. John G. Nicolay's The Outbreak of Rebellion (Scribner, 1881) is a retrospective history written, by its preface, largely from the Official War Records for 1861; it is not independent of the report families. Morris's June 7, 1861 report with its inclosed orders (Official Records Series I, Volume II) is one family of interested Union accounts. The Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
